transcript:
Header:
- Date: 2026-03-20
- Start: 15:30 UTC
- Duration: ~58 minutes
- Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Jordan (Redwood SE), Anika (Redwood CSM), Ethan (BlueCrest Platform), Priya (BlueCrest ML), Sofia (Head of AI), Liam (Security)

Auto-summary (auto-gen, may be rough):
Redwood and BlueCrest discuss POC to validate throughput and latency for a multimodal chat-and-summarization flow for logistics customer support & document parsing. Focus on QPS, concurrency, token mix, canary plan, security gating.

00:00 Maya Patel: hey everyone, thanks for joining, um, curious if you've got the calendar invite, we'll run about an hour, go through the traffic profile, desired SLAs, and propose a bench plan.
00:14 Ethan Brooks: yep thanks Maya. quick note, we're on a pretty tight timeline, execs want a demo in 4 weeks, POC ideally done in 3. I can walk through our current infra.
00:22 Jordan Liu: cool, i'll try to capture latency and token distro requirements. a couple clarifying q's up front — are you planning hosted or private during the POC?
00:30 Sofia Martinez: for POC we prefer Redwood hosted to move faster, but we need VPC peering for private data. if things look good we want private deployment on-prem later.
00:42 Liam O'Connor: security perspective: SOC2 type II important, we use AES-256 with KMS/HSM for keys, need audit logs, SSO SAML, RBAC. We'll go deeper on Wednesday.
00:58 Maya Patel: noted — we'll include SOC2 and KMS docs. quick question on workload: is this primarily chat-style requests or document summarization?
01:05 Priya Nair: it's mixed. about 60% quick chat (short prompts, 20-120 input tokens), 30% document summarization (longer inputs, attachments, avg input tokens 1,200, outputs 300-800), 10% reranking/rewrite tasks.
01:21 Jordan Liu: ok that token mix helps. do you have observed QPS/concurrency? e.g., peak QPS, average, and concurrent open sessions?
01:30 Ethan Brooks: our current microservice sees steady QPS of 12 during the day, peak bursts to 280 during batch arrivals from partners. Concurrency on our side is approx 40 active sessions on average, spikes to 380 during peaks. But the LLM call patterns are bursty — often a fanout pattern when summarizing 50 documents.
01:52 Maya Patel: so we should model both steady-state and burst scenarios. suggested POC matrix: steady-state 15-25 QPS, burst mode 250-300 QPS for 2–5 minutes. agree?
02:05 Sofia Martinez: yes. also we care about tail latency — p95 and p99. For chat, product wants p95 < 350ms, p99 < 900ms. For long summarizations p95 < 1.5s acceptable but p99 < 3s.
02:24 Jordan Liu: ok, we'll test two model variants: a cost-optimized quantized variant and a full-precision for quality. We'll capture token-throughput and per-token cost.
02:34 Priya Nair: how do you treat KV cache when we have session-based chat? we need KV to persist for multi-turn to keep context.
02:42 Jordan Liu: Redwood runtime supports persistent KV cache for sessions. for the POC we'll simulate session affinity to the same worker to measure cache hit rates and reduced latency. we'll also test cold-starts.
02:54 Ethan Brooks: nice. on tokens — our histogram: 55% of chat inputs < 80 tokens, 30% 80–240, 10% 240–1200, 5% >1200. outputs skew similar but summarization outputs average 450 tokens. I'll share the raw histograms.
03:12 Maya Patel: perfect, please attach that list. that will let us build synthetic request profiles.
03:18 Priya Nair: another concern — cost. we currently pay per GPU inference host, and need to approximate per-1000-token cost to compare. our finance expects cost justification.
03:27 Maya Patel: we'll include per-token cost modeling and a sensitivity analysis across batching settings and quantization. Jordan: plan to run multiple batch sizes.
03:34 Jordan Liu: yes. bench matrix will vary batch size, sequence length, and concurrency. we'll produce a qps vs latency curve, and per-1k token cost estimates assuming your traffic mix.
03:44 Liam O'Connor: about network topology: we require private peering and our data residency policy restricts PII leaving the VPC. can Redwood running on hosted mode support VPC peering or do we need Private?
03:57 Maya Patel: hosted can support VPC peering for select customers via Private Connect — for the POC we can do an encrypted tunnel and limited peering. for long term, Redwood Private gives you full VPC and on-prem options.
04:10 Liam O'Connor: we'll need to see the network architecture diagram and details of KMS integration.
04:16 Anika Shah: we'll schedule the security deep dive and share the diagrams.
04:22 Sofia Martinez: success criteria: 1) functional parity on summarization quality vs baseline (we'll share eval prompts), 2) performance: p95 targets met for chat and summarization, 3) cost target: below 60% increase vs current baseline or better ROI in 6 months, 4) reliability: can handle burst without dropping requests.
04:48 Jordan Liu: for quality we can run side-by-side evals — rouge/bleu or more likely LLM-based evals on your prompt set. can you provide the baseline model outputs for comparison?
04:58 Priya Nair: yes, i'll export. we use an in-house distill model for quick summaries; full quality baseline from vendor X. we'll produce example outputs.
05:08 Maya Patel: timeline check: recommended 3 stage POC across 3–4 weeks: week1 — ingest logs and create synthetic traffic; week2 — functional tests and small perf runs; week3 — full perf/burst tests and failure injection; week4 optional — resilience and canary rollout. is that acceptable?
05:26 Ethan Brooks: that aligns; exec demo target 4 weeks. we want a go/no-go after week3.
05:34 Jordan Liu: technically for benchmarks we'll set up harness with vegeta-style qps spikes, and include both open-loop and closed-loop tests to measure queueing effects. we'll capture latency distribution, GPU utilization, and token throughput.
05:48 Priya Nair: for open-loop tests, ensure you simulate our fanout summarization — e.g., 1 request triggers 50 downstream transforms. that was the main cause of our prior failures.
06:00 Jordan Liu: good point. we'll include cascade workloads in the bench. also include KV cache warm vs cold path.
06:08 Maya Patel: on metrics, we'll deliver a bench report with: p50/p95/p99 latencies, throughput (tokens/sec), GPU utilization, cost per 1k tokens, error rates, and recommendations.
06:20 Ethan Brooks: on scale, if POC passes, initial dedicated capacity target is 3x current peak — so plan for 900 concurrent spikes with automated burst to 1,200 for partner windows. can Redwood autoscale that fast?
06:36 Jordan Liu: Dedicated pools support fast autoscale and burst policies, but ramp time depends on capacity headroom. in the POC we'll exercise autoscale and measure ramp to target. we'll also show a fallback policy to smaller models to keep availability.
06:50 Liam O'Connor: fallback to a quantized smaller model is fine, but must preserve privacy and not send data to external vendors.
07:00 Maya Patel: noted. we'll show routing policy options and region-based fallbacks only inside your private tenancy.
07:06 Sofia Martinez: what's the expected noise from other tenants when hosted? we worry about noisy neighbor effects.
07:12 Jordan Liu: hosted uses isolation at scheduling level, but if you need stricter isolation we recommend Dedicated or Private. POC hosted mode will still emulate noise by running background workloads to validate isolation.
07:26 Priya Nair: benchmarks: for token distribution we want tests run at three seq-length profiles — chat-short (avg 60in/40out), medium (avg 300in/150out), long-doc (avg 1200in/450out). Run each at steady QPS 20 and bursts 250 for 3–5 minutes and measure p95/p99.
07:50 Jordan Liu: makes sense. we'll produce the QPS/concurrency matrix and include multi-model variants. Also recommend monitoring token emission rate and truncation counts as part of quality checks.
08:02 Ethan Brooks: question — what tooling will Redwood use for tracing / observability? we need request-level trace IDs passed through, and token-level cost breakdowns.
08:12 Anika Shah: Redwood Console provides per-request timing, token counts, and cost per route. we'll share screenshots and a sample dashboard.
08:20 Liam O'Connor: for audit, we need immutable logs and an exportable audit trail.
08:24 Anika Shah: yes, audit logs exportable to your SIEM, retention configurable.
08:30 Maya Patel: ok summary of deliverables: Redwood to deliver benchmark plan and scripts, cost model, security docs, and sample console dashboard. BlueCrest to deliver logs, prompt sets, and sample outputs. POC kickoff ideally next Monday.
08:44 Sofia Martinez: Can you confirm the POC signing — any MSA or scoping SOW?
08:49 Maya Patel: we'll send a short scoping SOW for signature capturing milestones. no heavy legal to start but if Private deployment then MSA required.
08:58 Ethan Brooks: fine. any blockers on our side? just getting the logs and legal signoff for peering.
09:04 Jordan Liu: one last technical note — when we run p99 for long-doc summarization, memory pressure on KV and GPU memory can increase due to context windows. we'll measure memory and recommend quantization or sharding strategies if needed.
09:22 Priya Nair: good — also include guidance on checkpointing retrievals and incremental summarization to lower peak memory.
09:33 Maya Patel: great feedback. we'll incorporate that.
09:38 Anika Shah: i'll own scheduling the security deep dive and send invites.
09:42 Maya Patel: any final questions?
09:44 Sofia Martinez: none, thanks everyone. excited to see the bench plan.
09:47 Maya Patel: thanks all — we'll follow up with the benchmark harness and SOW. talk soon.
